mcqs.q: The word 'interim' means:
opts: Established for the time being, pending a permanent arrangement
Made to last the lifetime of the tooth
Cemented with a definitive luting agent
mcqs.explain: Interim crowns are also called temporary or provisional restorations.

mcqs.q: The requirements of an interim restoration are grouped into:
mcqs.explain: Three groups of requirements are described.

mcqs.q: Pulpal protection requires that the interim restoration:
opts: Seals and insulates the prepared surface from the oral environment
Permits salivary exchange at the margin
Transmits thermal change to stimulate the pulp
Remains slightly short of the finish line
mcqs.explain: The aim is to prevent sensitivity and further irritation to the pulp.

mcqs.q: Which is listed as a PRESENT factor contributing to pulp death, during fixed prosthodontic therapy?
mcqs.explain: Caries, operative dentistry, bruxism, periodontal surgery and prosthodontic therapy are the PAST factors.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a 'present' factor contributing to pulp death during fixed prosthodontic therapy?
mcqs.explain: Operative dentistry belongs to the past column.

mcqs.q: To facilitate plaque removal, the interim restoration must have:
opts: Good marginal fit, proper contour and a smooth surface
mcqs.explain: Excess temporary luting agent must also be removed.

mcqs.q: Inadequate proximal and occlusal contacts around an interim restoration allow:
opts: Faster setting of the luting agent
mcqs.explain: The definitive restoration may then no longer fit the space planned for it.

mcqs.q: Prevention of enamel fracture is particularly important with:
opts: Partial coverage designs, where the margin is close to the occlusal surface
Full veneer crowns placed on second molars
mcqs.explain: The interim must protect teeth weakened by the crown preparation.

mcqs.q: Functional demand on an interim restoration is greater in:
opts: A fixed partial denture and partial coverage than full coverage
A full coverage crown than a fixed partial denture
A single anterior crown than a posterior bridge
An implant crown than a tooth-borne crown
mcqs.explain: The connector size may be increased, without harming the periodontium.

mcqs.q: A displaced interim restoration must be recemented promptly to avoid:
opts: Irritation to the pulp and tooth movement
mcqs.explain: Both consequences defeat the purpose of the interim.

mcqs.q: Excessive space between the interim restoration and the tooth is a problem because the luting agent:
opts: Has lower strength than regular cement and cannot tolerate the added force
Sets too quickly in a thick layer
mcqs.explain: Interim luting agents are deliberately weak so the restoration can be removed.

mcqs.q: An interim restoration usually survives removal intact provided that:
opts: The cement is sufficiently weak and the interim is well fabricated
The cement is as strong as a definitive cement
It has been relined at every visit
mcqs.explain: Interim restorations often need to be reused.

mcqs.q: Which is an esthetic requirement of an interim restoration?
mcqs.explain: Colour, size, shape, alignment, colour stability, and service as a guide for the permanent restoration.

mcqs.q: Interim restorations are classified by which two surfaces?
mcqs.explain: The external surface describes the form; the tissue surface describes where it was generated.

mcqs.q: Which is a PREFORMED resin crown form?
mcqs.explain: Cellulose acetate and polycarbonate are the resin forms; the others are metallic.

mcqs.q: Preformed crowns are generally limited to use as:
mcqs.explain: They must also be lined with autopolymerizing resin.

mcqs.q: Which modification is NOT listed as needed for a preformed crown?
opts: Addition of a cast metal post
mcqs.explain: The three listed modifications are internal relief, axial recontouring and occlusal adjustment.

mcqs.q: Polycarbonate crowns are described as having:
opts: The most natural appearance but only a single shade
A wide range of shades and high strength
A transparent shell that is peeled off
mcqs.explain: They are supplied in incisor, canine and premolar tooth types.

mcqs.q: Cellulose acetate shells are:
opts: Supplied in a wide shade range
mcqs.explain: Their shade depends entirely on the autopolymerizing resin used inside.

mcqs.q: After polymerization, a cellulose acetate shell is:
mcqs.explain: Removing the shell necessitates adding resin to re-establish proximal contacts.

mcqs.q: The disadvantage of peeling off the cellulose acetate shell is that it:
opts: Necessitates adding resin to re-establish proximal contacts
Changes the shade of the resin
mcqs.explain: The contacts are carried by the shell, so they must be rebuilt once it is removed.

mcqs.q: Aluminum and tin-silver crown forms are suitable for:
mcqs.explain: The most elaborate have anatomically shaped occlusal and axial surfaces.

mcqs.q: The most basic and least expensive metallic crown forms are described as:
opts: Cylindrical shells resembling a tin can
mcqs.explain: They require the most adaptation to approach an anatomic contour.

mcqs.q: Nickel-chromium crowns are primarily used for:
mcqs.explain: They are very hard and suit longer-term interim restorations.

mcqs.q: Unlike other preformed crowns, nickel-chromium crowns are:
opts: Not lined with resin — they are trimmed
Lined with two layers of resin
mcqs.explain: Their hardness is what makes them suitable for longer service.

mcqs.q: A custom external form is a negative reproduction of:
opts: The teeth before preparation or a modified diagnostic cast
The prepared teeth after reduction is complete
The opposing arch recorded in alginate
The edentulous ridge and the adjacent tissue
mcqs.explain: It is made of impression materials or a thermoplastic sheet.

mcqs.q: For a custom matrix, which impression material is preferred?
mcqs.explain: Putty materials are popular as they need no tray, are flexible and are easily trimmed.

mcqs.q: Putty matrix materials are popular because they:
opts: Can be used without a tray, are flexible and easily trimmed
Set faster than any other material
mcqs.explain: These handling advantages suit chairside matrix work.

mcqs.q: In the DIRECT procedure, the matrix material is seated:
opts: Directly on the patient's prepared teeth
On a diagnostic cast prepared in the lab
mcqs.explain: Its advantage is no need for lab support; its disadvantage is long chair-side time.

mcqs.q: The disadvantage of the direct procedure is:
opts: Irritation of the tooth by the cast
mcqs.explain: Everything is done in the mouth, which takes clinical time.

mcqs.q: In the INDIRECT procedure, the impression of the prepared teeth is poured in:
mcqs.explain: The interim is then built on that cast rather than in the mouth.

mcqs.q: An advantage of the indirect procedure is that it is:
opts: Not irritating to tooth and soft tissues — thermally, chemically and mechanically
Faster at the chairside than any other method
Able to use alginate matrices only
mcqs.explain: The exothermic, chemical and mechanical insults happen away from the patient.

mcqs.q: The disadvantage of the indirect procedure is:
mcqs.explain: The trade-off is laboratory turnaround against clinical comfort.

mcqs.q: In the INDIRECT–DIRECT procedure, the diagnostic cast is made:
mcqs.explain: The teeth are then prepared on the cast with minimal reduction in the lab.

mcqs.q: In the indirect–direct procedure, the final step at the chairside is to:
opts: Line the interim with resin on the patient's teeth
Mill the restoration from a disc
mcqs.explain: The bulk is made in the lab and only the thin lining is done in the mouth.

mcqs.q: In the CAD-CAM workflow, what is taken after tooth preparation?
opts: A scan or an alginate impression
A putty matrix of the unprepared teeth
mcqs.explain: The record is then designed (CAD) and milled (CAM).

mcqs.q: In CAD-CAM, 'CAM' refers to the:
mcqs.explain: CAD is the design; CAM is the manufacture.

mcqs.q: Which is an ideal property of an interim material?
opts: High exothermic reaction for rapid set
Maximum abrasiveness against the opposing tooth
mcqs.explain: Biocompatibility requires it to be nontoxic, nonallergenic and nonexothermic.

mcqs.q: Under biocompatibility, an interim material should be:
mcqs.explain: An exothermic set would injure the pulp it is meant to protect.

mcqs.q: Which handling property is listed as ideal?
opts: Adequate working time, easy molding and rapid setting
A long setting time to allow adjustment
mcqs.explain: Convenient handling is the first of the ideal properties.

mcqs.q: Which is listed among the available interim materials?
mcqs.explain: PMMA, poly(R methacrylate), microfilled composite and fibre-reinforced composite are the listed materials.

mcqs.q: Microfilled composite is listed as being used with which technique?
mcqs.explain: It is specified as a direct-technique material.

mcqs.q: An ideal interim material should be chemically compatible with:
mcqs.explain: Incompatibility would compromise retention or set of the luting agent.

saqs.q: Define an interim restoration and list the three groups of requirements.
saqs.a: Interim crowns or partial fixed dental prostheses are essential in prosthodontic therapy. INTERIM means established for the time being, pending a permanent arrangement; they are also called temporary or provisional. The requirements fall into three groups: BIOLOGIC, MECHANICAL and ESTHETIC.

ans.text: Interim crowns or partial fixed dental prostheses are essential in prosthodontic therapy. Interim means established for the time being, pending a permanent arrangement — also called temporary or provisional.

saqs.q: Outline the four biologic requirements of an interim restoration.
saqs.a: PULPAL PROTECTION — it must seal and insulate the prepared tooth surface from the oral environment, to prevent sensitivity and further irritation to the pulp. PERIODONTAL HEALTH — to facilitate plaque removal it must have good marginal fit, proper contour and a smooth surface, and excess temporary luting must be removed. OCCLUSAL COMPATIBILITY AND TOOTH POSITION — it should maintain proper contacts with adjacent and opposing teeth, because inadequate contacts allow supra-eruption and horizontal movement. PREVENTION OF ENAMEL FRACTURE — it should protect teeth weakened by the crown preparation, particularly with partial coverage designs where the margin is close to the occlusal surface.

head: Requirement
What it means
rows: seal and insulate the prepared surface from the oral environment — preventing sensitivity and further pulpal irritation
good marginal fit, proper contour, smooth surface to allow plaque removal; excess luting must be removed
maintain proper contacts with adjacent and opposing teeth — inadequate contacts allow supra-eruption and horizontal movement
protect teeth weakened by the preparation — particularly in partial coverage designs where the margin lies close to the occlusal surface

saqs.q: Give the factors contributing to pulp death, past and present.
saqs.a: PAST — caries, operative dentistry, bruxism, periodontal surgery and prosthodontic therapy. PRESENT, during fixed prosthodontic therapy — preparation trauma, microbial exposure, desiccation, chemical exposure and thermal exposure.

saqs.q: Outline the mechanical requirements of an interim restoration.
saqs.a: FUNCTION — the demand is greater in a fixed partial denture and in partial coverage than in full coverage; connector size may be increased without harming the periodontium. DISPLACEMENT — a displaced interim must be recemented promptly if pulpal irritation and tooth movement are to be avoided, and excessive space between restoration and tooth places greater demands on the luting agent, which has lower strength than regular cement and cannot tolerate the added force. REMOVAL FOR REUSE — interims often need to be reused and so should not be damaged on removal; in most instances, if the cement is sufficiently weak and the interim well fabricated, it does not break.

a displaced interim must be recemented promptly or the pulp is irritated and the tooth moves

ans.text: Excessive space between restoration and tooth puts greater demand on the luting agent, which has lower strength than regular cement and cannot tolerate the added force.

saqs.q: Classify interim restorations by external surface form.
saqs.a: A) PREFORMED — resin (cellulose acetate, polycarbonate) and metallic (aluminum, tin-silver, nickel-chromium). B) CUSTOM — elastomer and thermoplastic sheet. A custom form is a negative reproduction of either the patient's teeth before preparation or a modified diagnostic cast; elastomers are preferable to alginate, and putty materials are popular because they can be used without a tray, are flexible and are easily trimmed.

ans.text: A custom form is a negative reproduction of either the patient's teeth before preparation or a modified diagnostic cast. Elastomers are preferable to alginate, and putty is popular because it needs no tray, is flexible and is easily trimmed.

saqs.q: Compare the four preformed crown materials.
saqs.a: POLYCARBONATE — the most natural appearance, only a single shade, supplied in incisor, canine and premolar types. CELLULOSE ACETATE — thin (0.2–0.3 mm) and transparent, shades depending entirely on the autopolymerizing resin; the shell is peeled off after polymerization, which necessitates adding resin to re-establish proximal contacts. ALUMINUM AND TIN-SILVER — suitable for posterior teeth; the most elaborate forms have anatomically shaped occlusal and axial surfaces, while the most basic and least expensive are merely cylindrical shells resembling a tin can. NICKEL-CHROMIUM — primarily for children, not lined with resin but trimmed, and very hard so they can be used for longer-term interim restorations.

head: Material
Characteristics

ans.text: All preformed crowns are generally limited to single restorations, must be lined with autopolymerizing resin (except nickel-chromium), and need internal relief, axial recontouring and occlusal adjustment.

saqs.q: Describe the three tissue-surface procedures with their advantages and disadvantages.
saqs.a: DIRECT — after tooth preparation the putty or thermoplastic material is seated directly on the patient's teeth; advantage: no need for lab support; disadvantage: long chair-side time. INDIRECT — an impression is made of the prepared teeth and ridge tissue and poured in quick-setting gypsum; advantages: not irritating to tooth and soft tissues thermally, chemically and mechanically, and less chair-side procedure; disadvantage: needs lab support. INDIRECT–DIRECT — a diagnostic cast is made before tooth preparation, the teeth are prepared on the cast with minimal reduction in the lab, the interim is fabricated on the cast indirectly, and after tooth preparation it is lined with resin on the patient's teeth.

saqs.q: List the ideal properties of a material for interim fixed restorations.
saqs.a: Convenient handling — adequate working time, easy molding, rapid setting time. Biocompatibility — nontoxic, nonallergenic, nonexothermic. Dimensional stability during solidification. Ease of contouring and polishing. Adequate strength and abrasion resistance. Good appearance — translucent, colour controllable, colour stable. Good acceptability to the patient — nonirritating, odourless. Ease of adding to or repairing. Chemical compatibility with interim luting agents.

list: Convenient handling — adequate working time, easy molding, rapid setting time
Good appearance — translucent, colour controllable, colour stable
Good acceptability to the patient — nonirritating, odourless

saqs.q: Name the available interim materials and outline the CAD-CAM workflow.
saqs.a: MATERIALS — poly(methyl methacrylate), poly(R methacrylate), microfilled composite (direct technique) and fibre-reinforced composite. CAD-CAM — after tooth preparation take a scan or an alginate impression, send it for designing (CAD), then milling (CAM).
